after: Pruning is performed by the daemon and by nothing else, and each removal appends a `payload.pruned` event, so a log states what its store no longer holds. The bytes an attestation binds (§5.2, §10.4) are never prunable while that attestation is the one in force: they are not bound to an action and have no terminal state, and the policy in force binds them exactly as a live approval binds its own material. (Policy vocabulary in v0.1; enforcement lands with the M5 daemon. The attestation sentence is APRV-356.)
